description: What total of credit support and minimum-revenue guarantees to AI labs and cloud partners will NVIDIA disclose at its next annual report?
outcome: The disclosed amount of guarantees, credit-support commitments and revenue backstops NVIDIA has extended to AI labs and cloud partners (including the credit support for nearly 2 gigawatts of computing capacity for one additional AI lab), versus the equity investments it has made, at NVIDIA's next annual report.
period: Fiscal 2027 annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027; Form 10-K expected around February 2027) — set as the next annual report following this 22 September 2026 item, per section 3 (obligation already undertaken tracked by its amount at the next annual report; the additional AI lab's credit support is not yet signed and is checked within 18 months).

description: How much will NVIDIA disclose in purchase and supply commitments (obligations to buy capacity, components or services) at its next annual report?
outcome: The amount of purchase obligations/supply commitments NVIDIA reports in its contractual obligations and purchase commitment disclosures in the Form 10-K, versus the prior year, given the analyst report that NVIDIA is taking on larger supply commitments.
period: Fiscal 2027 annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027; Form 10-K expected around February 2027) — the next annual report after this 22 September 2026 item, per section 3 (an obligation already undertaken is tracked by its amount at the next annual report).

description: Will Nvidia be permitted to sell its current Blackwell-generation AI chips into China — through U.S. export approval and Chinese acceptance of shipments — by the end of fiscal 2027?
outcome: Whether U.S. authorities extend export approval beyond the older H200 to Nvidia's current Blackwell-generation chips for approved Chinese customers, and whether Chinese authorities stop restricting Nvidia chip shipments, so that China data-center revenue can resume; the item reports H200 shipments are already U.S.-permitted while Chinese authorities still restrict them.
period: NVIDIA fiscal year ending late January 2027 — the current fiscal year-end, used as the check date for a pending regulatory decision per section 3 (item gives no date of its own).

description: Will NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI platform, which the company says has entered full production, reach volume customer shipments (first revenue recognition) by the end of fiscal 2027?
outcome: Whether Vera Rubin moves from full production to volume customer shipments and first revenue recognition within NVIDIA's fiscal 2027, as shown in the company's quarterly results and Form 10-K.
period: NVIDIA fiscal year ending late January 2027 (FY2027), checked at NVIDIA's quarterly results and FY2027 Form 10-K. The item gives no shipment date; the current fiscal year-end following the September 2026 report that Vera Rubin entered full production is used as the check date.

description: How much will the five largest AI hyperscalers spend in total on data centers in calendar 2026?
outcome: The big five AI hyperscalers' combined calendar-2026 data center capital expenditure, compared with the nearly $800 billion the article says they will spend this year.
period: Calendar year 2026 (the item's 'this year' in a 23 September 2026 article), checked at the hyperscalers' Q4/full-year 2026 earnings and capex disclosures in early 2027.

description: Will NVIDIA complete its approximately $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, agreed in 2026, by the check date?
outcome: Whether the agreed ~$12.9 billion Hugging Face acquisition is signed and closed (completed) as disclosed in NVIDIA's filings, versus being repriced, delayed past the check date or terminated.
period: Check date 24 March 2028 (18 months after the 25 September 2026 item) — set per section 3 for a sized acquisition not yet completed, because the item gives no signing or closing date; also observable in NVIDIA's quarterly filings before then.

description: Will China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology formally approve purchases of Nvidia's new RTX Pro 5500 high-end GPU by Alibaba, ByteDance and other Chinese firms by the end of Nvidia's fiscal 2027, allowing those sales to proceed?
outcome: Whether MIIT moves from signaling intent and collecting purchase plans to actually approving Alibaba's, ByteDance's and other Chinese firms' purchases of the RTX Pro 5500 (versus blocking, delaying or capping quantities), so that Nvidia can ship the product into China and book related revenue.
period: NVIDIA fiscal year ending late January 2027 — the current fiscal year-end used as the check date for a pending regulatory decision per section 3, because the item gives no date of its own.
